title: Grimoire character sheet
description: A schema-driven character sheet: the fields a character has, the values derived from them, and how the sheet is drawn. Grimoire renders any sheet here without game-specific code.

id.description: Lowercase, hyphenated; must match the directory name.

system.description: The game this sheet is for, shown in the picker. Display-only.

author.description: Who wrote this sheet. A GitHub username (e.g. 'hunter-read') links to that profile in Grimoire; any other text is credited without a link.

license.description: The licence the sheet's content is published under (e.g. 'CC-BY-4.0', 'ORC', 'Draw Steel Creator License').

attribution.description: Credit for the upstream game, rendered verbatim in Grimoire wherever this sheet is browsed or used. Some licences require exact wording — reproduce it here character for character.

fields.description: The editable state of a character, keyed by field name.

options.description: Required for type 'select'. Either plain values or {value, label} objects.

visible_if.description: An expression; the field is drawn only when it is true. A condition that cannot be evaluated shows the field, because hiding part of a sheet over a broken expression would cost the player access to their own data.

default_from.description: An expression giving this field's value until the player sets one - e.g. ref(species, 'speed'). The player can always type over it, and reset it back. May read fields but not computed values, which are worked out after it. An empty result falls back to 'default'.

on_pick.description: content_ref only. What picking an entry does to other fields. Everything a pick adds is recorded, so changing the pick takes it back off. The player can still edit the result freely.

oneOf.description: Add values from the picked entry. Into a multiselect: 'from' names a list property. Into a content_list: 'ref' names an entry id, falling back to 'name' as a freeform entry when the catalog has no such entry.
Ask the player to choose 'count' values from the entry's 'from' list, into a multiselect.

choose.description: The multiselect field to choose into.

from.description: The picked entry's property to read values or options from.

ref.description: The picked entry's property holding an entry id to grant.

name.description: The picked entry's property holding a name to grant when the id is not installed.

count.description: How many to choose: a number, or the name of the picked entry's property holding it.

label.description: The prompt shown for a choice.

columns.description: Required for type 'list'. Each column is a field definition with a 'key'. A column may be any scalar type but not another list.

content_type.description: Required for content_ref/content_list: the content type this field picks from. Must be one the schema declares.

per_entry_fields.description: The character's own notes on a referenced entry — prepared, equipped, uses remaining. Ordinary field definitions.

allow_freeform.description: Lets a player type an entry instead of picking one, so the catalog stays optional.

display_columns.description: content_list only. Draw the list as a table of these properties of each picked entry - a spell's level, casting time and range - rather than a name and a one-line summary.

computed.description: Values derived from fields. Read-only, recalculated on every read, never stored.

formula.description: An expression over other fields. Arithmetic, comparison, logic, and the closed function table: floor, ceil, round, abs, min, max, sum, len, if, clamp, signed. Parsed, never executed.

layout.description: The simple sheet: sections of fields, drawn in a responsive grid. Omit it (and layout_html) and Grimoire lists every field in declaration order.

visible_if.description: The whole section is drawn only when this expression is true.

layout_html.description: A custom sheet as an HTML template, written inline. Prefer 'layout_file' for anything longer than a line or two — HTML embedded in JSON has to be escaped, which makes it unreadable and unmaintainable.

styles.description: CSS for the layout, written inline. Prefer 'styles_file' for anything substantial.

validators.description: Rules checked against a character. A rule states what should be true, so a false result is reported. They never block saving.

content_types.description: Typed catalogs a character can reference — spells, classes, feats. A content type is a field schema applied to entries rather than to a character.

identity_field.description: The entry's name — what a reference shows and what the catalog sorts by. Must be one of the type's own fields.

compact_display.description: A one-line template like '{name} — {school} {level}'. Every {token} must name one of the type's fields.

layout_file.description: A sibling .html file holding the layout, instead of inlining it. Defaults to '<id>.html' when that file exists. This is how a real sheet should be written: the HTML stays HTML, with syntax highlighting and no escaping.

styles_file.description: A sibling .css file holding the stylesheet, instead of inlining it. Defaults to '<id>.css' when that file exists.

name_field.description: A text field that holds the character's name. It starts as the name given when the character is created, and editing either one updates the other.
